settings.intro: Spend a moment with the people, places, and handwork behind the collection.

settings.title: Hand-block printing
settings.story: A carved wooden block is dipped in colour and pressed onto the cloth. The printer repeats the impression to build the pattern. Look closely at Gulnaar’s flowers: small changes in colour and placement are part of block printing by hand.

settings.title: Chikankari hand embroidery
settings.story: Chikankari is a hand embroidery tradition from Lucknow, India. Artisans use a needle and thread to stitch delicate flowers and vines into the cloth. On Noor Bagh, fine stitches form vines and flowers across the raw silk. The ivory and gold-toned threads make the needlework easy to see against the beige fabric.

settings.title: Raised hand embroidery
settings.story: Zardozi is a hand embroidery technique with ornate, raised stitching. Desert Pearl pairs this detailing with raw silk and a tasselled drawstring. The same technique appears on several of our statement bags and children’s occasion sets.

settings.title: Ayurveda (Wellness)
settings.story: Rooted in Indian traditions of everyday care, this collection brings together hair oils, shampoo, masks and body care. Take a little time to oil your hair before washing, or work a body oil into your routine. Explore the ingredients and directions on each product to find what fits your day.
